newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-GREAT COMEBACK GIVES BARCELONA 4-2 WIN AT BETIS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GREAT COMEBACK GIVES BARCELONA 4-2 WIN AT BETIS.

text.p: A hat-trick of headers by midfielder Luis Enrique Martinez saved manager Bobby Robson on Sunday as Barcelona came back from 2-0 down to win 4-2 in a sensational game at Real Betis.

With memories of a shock defeat by Hercules still fresh, the former England coach's job was undoubtedly on the line. But the victory left Barcelona within three points of leaders Real Madrid and could well have put new life into a side badly needing a confidence boost.
The result -- and the inspirational style of Barcelona's recovery -- followed Real's own extraordinary 4-1 win at neighbours Atletico on Saturday.
And with Deportivo Coruna slipping up at home, Spain's league championship once again seems to be at the mercy of the country's 'old firm'.

Betis went ahead on the half-hour when Croatian midfielder Robert Jarni snaked a long-range free-kick through the Barcelona defence. Three minutes later the southerners went two-up when defender Sergi Barjuan turned a cross from Jarni into his own net.
But Barcelona fought back and pulled a goal back on the stroke of halftime when Luis Enrique was left unmarked at a corner.
Twenty minutes into the second half of a game played at breakneck pace in wet conditions Josep Guardiola left the Betis defence flat-footed and Luis Enrique was again on hand to head home.

Shortly afterwards three defenders waiting for a trademark run from Ronaldo were dazzled when the Brazilian striker unleashed a powerful shot from the edge of the area which gave Betis keeper Toni Prats no chance.
Luis Enrique headed the fourth after more sloppy defending at a corner 12 minutes from time.

Four points behind Barcelona are Deportivo Coruna, whose fans jeered their British coach John Toshack on Sunday after his multi-billion peseta side lost ground on the leaders with a poor 2-2 draw at home to Athletic Bilbao.

Toshack's side started well when Donato converted a fourth-minute penalty. But the Welsh coach earned the wrath of the crowd at the Riazor stadium shortly afterwards by taking off another Brazilian midfielder, Rivaldo.
Toshack was seen to mouth comments back to the fans, and club chairman Augusto Lendoiro had to speak to both manager and players at halftime.
Athletic's Julen Guerrero rounded off a bad afternoon for Deportivo by scoring a late equaliser.
Real Sociedad took fourth place from Betis thanks to two Javi de Pedro penalties in a comfortable 4-1 win over Compostela.
As a result reigning champions Atletico Madrid slipped to sixth, 11 points off the pace.
On a day on which four of the bottom seven sides won, struggling Zaragoza wasted a hatful of chances and missed a penalty before clinching a late equaliser in their home game with Tenerife.
Zaragoza are bottom but one, three points ahead of Extremadura, who clocked up their second victory of the season with a solitary goal at Celta Vigo.
Hercules followed up Monday's win at Barcelona with a confident display in a 1-0 home win over Valladolid, who dropped to seventh.
Valencia's recent recovery came to an abrupt halt in the opening 22 minutes of their game at Oviedo.

That was the time needed for the referee to show red cards to defender Francisco Ferreira -- sent off for blocking Toni Velamazan's route to goal -- and Russian midfielder Valery Karpin, who demonstrated his command of Spanish by swearing at a match official.
Valencia lost the game 3-0.
